target.title: refactor(qa): enforce surface.feature coverage IDs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves two related QA coverage identity problems. First, 158 semantic IDs were assigned to multiple taxonomy features, so reports could not identify one exact owner. Second, collision-qualified IDs could grow to three dot-separated parts even though the implementation performs exact string matching, making IDs such as `surface.feature.context` look hierarchical when they were not.

## Why This Change Was Made

Coverage IDs now have one canonical shape: `<surface-id>.<feature-id>`. Every taxonomy feature owns exactly one globally unique ID, and that ID's first segment must match its containing taxonomy surface. Broad rows that previously owned multiple semantic claims are split into atomic feature rows, so scenario YAML can reference only the exact feature its executable proves.

This keeps one vocabulary and one ownership path: taxonomy defines semantic IDs; scenario YAML maps executables to those IDs. There are no aliases, fallback readers, compatibility names, TypeScript eligibility registries, or implied parent/child coverage. A scenario covering `surface.feature-context` does not cover `surface.feature` unless it explicitly lists both exact IDs.

The original collision migration and its profile reconciliation remain part of the same atomic change. The fixed 12-scenario CI smoke plan remains unchanged, while `smoke-ci` narrows from 30 categories to the 10 categories that plan actually proves.

## User Impact

No OpenClaw runtime behavior changes. Maintainers and QA operators get unambiguous, flat coverage identities; truthful scenario-to-feature evidence; and selectors/profiles that reflect executable product proof. Internal QA coverage references are renamed to the strict two-part contract.

## Evidence

- Original current-main reconciliation: 1,992 taxonomy assignments before and after; 158 colliding source IDs across 479 assignments; 321 excess assignments migrated; all 395 previously affected scenario occurrences re-evaluated; zero unresolved/high-risk rows, duplicate targets, unknown targets, new last-primary losses, or zero-coverage scenarios.
- Strict two-part reconciliation: 1,676 broad feature rows -> 1,992 atomic feature rows; 92 multi-ID features -> 0; 260 three-part IDs -> 0; 1,461 wrong-surface prefixes -> 0; 1,717 IDs renamed and 275 already canonical. The catalog retains 351 scenarios and 552 exact references; 404 references across 246 scenarios were retargeted with zero unknown references.
- The strict rewrite preserves primary/secondary roles and the 1,992-claim denominator. Before/after category-identity and profile hashes are identical for this second normalization. Ignored detailed JSON SHA-256: `40fafb9c11c9aa863efe4c4121be99139e8234dce0aaa75c86cd422159095128` (base `9dec7acc91f00d8d8bbe39005e016e511181a9ca`, head `87a911dafdfa05dfb6af2534e3212c538bf1d309`).
- Profile deltas from the collision migration remain intentional semantic narrowing: `smoke-ci` 30 -> 10 categories; 148 scenarios leave smoke, 62 leave release, and none gain a profile. All 12 explicit smoke scenarios still resolve and cover every remaining smoke category.
- Blacksmith Testbox focused proof: initial complete owner/producer set 247/247 passed; restored sensitive-path catalog/taxonomy/profile set 173/173 passed; final rebased head taxonomy/catalog/scorecard/profile/script-evidence/workflow-guard set 271/271 passed. Final run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29628182428.
- Exact-path `pnpm check:changed` passed repository guards, formatting, SDK/API, dependency, database-first, and full TypeScript gates. Its sole lint finding (`no-map-spread`) was corrected; post-fix exact oxlint reports 0 warnings/errors and the affected owner test passes 15/15 on supported Node.
- Fresh Codex autoreview (`gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning) reviewed the 911 KB admissible diff in three complete bounded passes: zero findings; `patch is correct` (0.91 confidence). Four sensitive-filename YAML edits were restored afterward and independently revalidated by the audit and 173-test catalog suite.
- No migration-named test/artifact or historical-count registry is tracked. Existing owning tests enforce global uniqueness, known-reference integrity, exact two-part shape, one ID per feature, surface ownership, role constraints, and current smoke/profile behavior.
- AI-assisted; I inspected the affected taxonomy, catalog, selectors, scorecard/report projections, evidence producers, tests, and the previously required sibling Codex protocol boundaries, and I understand the resulting mappings.

target.title: test(plugin-sdk): cover origin trust SSRF edges
target.body:
## Summary

Adds the remaining origin-trust SSRF edge coverage and plugin SDK docs requested by #81963.

## Issue / Motivation

Fixes #81963.

The core origin-scoped SSRF behavior already landed in #80751. The follow-up issue asks for narrow provider `baseUrl` normalization coverage plus documentation of the trust semantics for plugin authors, without changing runtime policy.

## Changes

- Add regression coverage for provider `baseUrl` origin normalization:
  - trailing slash/path ignored for origin trust
  - default HTTP/HTTPS ports elided
  - userinfo stripped by `URL.origin`
  - configured trailing-dot hosts match their dotless request origin
- Add a concurrent isolation test showing overlapping private origins with different ports do not leak trust between configured base URLs.
- Document exact-origin trust semantics in `docs/plugins/sdk-subpaths.md`, including redirect re-evaluation and continued metadata/link-local/private-network resolver blocking.

## Testing

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/infra/net/ssrf.test.ts`
  - 57 tests passed on the previous head; exact-head local rerun is unavailable in the low-disk worktree because workspace dependencies are not installed, so exact-head CI is the runtime-test authority
- `pnpm oxfmt --check src/infra/net/ssrf.test.ts docs/plugins/sdk-subpaths.md`
  - All matched files use the correct format.
- `git diff --check`
  - passed
- staged diff secret scan
  - no secret-like added lines

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin/provider authors need a precise contract for when configured `baseUrl` values may promote a private hostname through the SSRF guard. This PR pins the intended origin-normalization behavior in tests and documents that the trust is exact-origin, per-request, and does not bypass resolver-level metadata/link-local/private network protections.

## Evidence

Exact-head static validation passed: `npx --yes oxfmt@latest --check docs/plugins/sdk-subpaths.md src/infra/net/ssrf.test.ts`, `npx --yes oxlint@latest --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/infra/net/ssrf.test.ts`, `node scripts/generate-docs-map.mjs --check`, `git diff --check`, and diff secret scan. The new regression directly covers the configured trailing-dot baseUrl contract identified in review. The PR intentionally contains tests/docs only and does not change production SSRF policy behavior.

target.title: feat(ios): add reference-inspired phone shell
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The iOS application currently exposes the gateway, assistant, voice, and settings capabilities through screens that do not share a clear phone-first visual hierarchy. The onboarding, connection state, and main navigation also feel visually disconnected, which makes the product harder to understand at a glance.

This PR introduces a cohesive iPhone shell inspired by the supplied six-screen reference while keeping OpenClaw's existing state, navigation, and gateway behavior intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The redesign gives the iOS client a consistent, native presentation across the complete first-run and connected experience:

- a branded red splash screen using the supplied OpenClaw artwork;
- a focused pairing screen with QR and manual setup actions;
- an Activity surface backed by real gateway, agent, session, and background-task state;
- a unified Assistant surface with Chat and Talk modes;
- a settings home that preserves the existing diagnostic and configuration routes;
- a compact floating navigation capsule shared by the connected phone layouts.

The implementation deliberately keeps the current iPad presentation unchanged. Connected phone tabs remain mounted while switching so chat and voice state are not discarded. Screenshot fixtures are isolated behind UI-test launch arguments and do not introduce production mock data.

This is a stacked PR targeting `ios-unified-chat-voice` (the branch for #107879) because it builds directly on that unified assistant foundation.

## User Impact

- New users see a clearer branded launch and pairing path.
- Connected users can move between Activity, Assistant, and Settings from a consistent bottom control.
- Assistant users can switch between the existing live chat and talk experiences without losing state.
- Gateway status, agent activity, approvals, sessions, and tasks continue to reflect real application state.
- Existing settings destinations, diagnostics, reconnect controls, and iPad behavior remain available.
- Accessibility labels and stable UI-test identifiers cover the new navigation and screenshot states.

## Evidence

### Automated verification

- `RootTabsSourceGuardTests`: **56 passed**
- `OpenClawLogicTests`: **44 passed** across 7 suites
- `OpenClawSnapshotUITests/testConnectedGatewayTabs`: **1 passed**, exercising all six reference states (splash, pairing, Activity, Talk, Chat, and Settings)
- SwiftFormat: **0 of 326 files require formatting**
- SwiftLint with `--no-cache`: **passed**
- `git diff --check`: **passed**
- Three local autoreview cycles completed; all actionable findings were resolved and covered by focused regression guards.

### Visual verification

The six-screen matrix was captured from a dedicated iPhone simulator and manually compared against the supplied reference for layout, spacing, typography, color, icon treatment, surface hierarchy, and navigation state. No generated screenshots are committed to the repository.

### Repository-wide runner note

A monolithic local `OpenClawTests` invocation was also attempted. It did not reach a terminal result because pre-existing gateway integration cases continuously retried an intentionally unavailable `127.0.0.1:1` endpoint. The modified-area guards, logic suites, and complete six-screen UI flow all terminate and pass; GitHub CI remains the authoritative repository-wide validation.

target.title: fix: separate allowPluginSyntheticAuth from allowAuthProfileFallback in model auth
target.body:
## Summary

修复了 gateway 路由的模型调用无法解析插件合成认证（如 Anthropic Vertex 的 ADC）的问题。

## Root Cause

在 `src/agents/model-auth.ts:1646`，当 `allowAuthProfileFallback: false` 时（gateway 准备的路径调用），`allowPluginSyntheticAuth` 也被错误地设置为 `false`：

```typescript
allowPluginSyntheticAuth: params.allowAuthProfileFallback !== false,
```

这导致 `resolveSyntheticLocalProviderAuth` 跳过插件合成认证解析，因此插件的 `resolveSyntheticAuth` hook 根本没有机会执行。

## Fix

- 添加独立的 `allowPluginSyntheticAuth` 参数到 `resolveApiKeyForProvider` 和 `getApiKeyForModel` 函数
- 默认值为 `true`（通过 `?? true`），而不是从 `allowAuthProfileFallback` 派生
- 分离了两个概念：
  1. `allowAuthProfileFallback` - 是否允许从 auth-profiles.json 读取存储的用户配置 profile
  2. `allowPluginSyntheticAuth` - 是否允许调用插件的 `resolveSyntheticAuth` hook

## Testing

添加了回归测试证明：
- 当 `allowAuthProfileFallback: false` 但 `allowPluginSyntheticAuth` 未指定（默认 true）时，插件合成认证成功解析
- 当 `allowPluginSyntheticAuth: false` 明确设置时，插件合成认证被阻止

## Related Issues

Fixes: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/110103

target.title: fix: order ambient transcript watermarks by decimal ids

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ambient transcript watermarks could treat non-decimal message ids such as `0x12` or `1e3` as ordered numbers when multiple messages share the same timestamp. That could advance or suppress the watermark using a numeric interpretation the channel did not actually provide.

## Why This Change Was Made

Watermark comparison now uses numeric ordering only for canonical non-negative decimal integer message ids. Other ids use a stable string boundary in both watermark persistence and Telegram history filtering, so equal-timestamp replay cannot move the stored boundary backward just because a different non-decimal id appears.

## User Impact

Users and operators get more reliable ambient transcript replay boundaries for channels that emit message ids that look numeric but are not canonical decimal integers.

target.title: fix(browser): cap fields-file reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser CLI action commands accept `--fields-file` for form field descriptors. The previous reader loaded the whole file into memory before validating or parsing it, so a very large fields file could be fully buffered before the CLI rejected it.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a narrow 1 MiB byte cap to the `--fields-file` path only. The reader consumes at most the cap plus one sentinel byte, rejects oversized files before JSON parsing, and leaves inline `--fields` behavior unchanged.

## User Impact

Users get a friendly size-limit error for oversized Browser CLI fields files instead of the CLI buffering arbitrarily large input. Existing valid fields files and inline JSON fields continue to work.

target.title: fix(update): prevent compatible plugins from being skipped after npm-global upgrades
target.body:
Refs #93908

## Summary

- Pin current-process post-core plugin compatibility checks to the installed target OpenClaw version for upgrades as well as downgrades.
- Pass that installed target version into mandatory post-core plugin convergence instead of overwriting the compatibility context with the stale updater-process `VERSION`.
- Preserve current `main`'s ClawHub risk-acknowledgement plumbing while keeping the installed target as the compatibility source of truth.
- Add focused regression coverage for the reported `2026.5.28` → `2026.6.8` Feishu/plugin API compatibility path.

## What Problem This Solves

An npm-global update replaces the installed OpenClaw package before the updater process exits. During that window, post-core plugin convergence can evaluate retained plugins against the updater's stale pre-update `VERSION` instead of the installed target version. A plugin that is compatible with the target gateway can therefore be skipped before restart. This patch makes the update handoff use the installed target version consistently, matching the host that will own the plugin after restart.

## User Impact

After an npm-global core update, the still-running updater process can report its pre-update version while the installed package and the gateway that will restart are already newer. A retained plugin compatible with the installed target can therefore be rejected during post-core convergence. In the reported path, Feishu `2026.6.8` is skipped as incompatible with stale host `2026.5.28`, leaving the channel unavailable even though core `2026.6.8` is installed.

This patch makes update-owned compatibility decisions use the installed target version that will run after restart. It does not relax compatibility ranges or add a Feishu-specific exception.

## Root Cause

Fresh post-core child processes already receive `OPENCLAW_COMPATIBILITY_HOST_VERSION=<installed target>`, but the current-process path previously pinned that value only for downgrades. Mandatory convergence also replaced inherited compatibility-host state with the updater module's stale `VERSION`.

The canonical source of truth during post-core update convergence is the installed target package version, because that is the host version that will own the plugin after restart. The patch passes that value through the existing compatibility resolver boundary and restores the caller's environment after the scoped phase.

If the installed target version cannot be read, convergence retains the existing fallback to runtime `VERSION`.

## What Did Not Change

- Feishu package metadata and `openclaw.compat.pluginApi` requirements.
- Semver compatibility enforcement or plugin manifest parsing.
- Default plugin installation policy or ClawHub trust/risk acknowledgement.
- Runtime behavior for genuinely incompatible plugins.
- General runtime host-version discovery outside the npm-global update handoff.

The last point is why this PR now uses `Refs #93908` rather than closing syntax: the issue also contains a distinct post-restart `unknown_host_version` reproduction that this update-scoped patch does not resolve.

## Evidence

### Real npm-global update and retained-plugin lifecycle

A disposable Windows environment used an isolated npm prefix, HOME, state directory, config and gateway port. `OPENCLAW_COMPATIBILITY_HOST_VERSION` was unset for the actual update. No external Feishu credentials were used because the behavior under test is package compatibility, retention and discovery rather than network delivery.

1. Installed the real npm package `openclaw@2026.5.28` into the isolated global prefix:

   ```text
   OpenClaw 2026.5.28 (e932160)
   ```

2. Installed and retained the real npm plugin `@openclaw/feishu@2026.6.8`. With the compatibility override absent, the baseline production CLI reproduced the stale-host rejection:

   ```text
   plugin requires OpenClaw >=2026.5.29, but this host is 2026.5.28; skipping load
   ```

3. Ran the real production update command against a target `2026.6.8` package carrying this PR's emitted update-path changes:

   ```text
   openclaw update --yes --timeout 600
   ```

   The command performed the real managed-gateway stop and npm-global replacement:

   ```text
   Updating OpenClaw...
   Stopping managed gateway service before package update...

   Update Result: OK
     Before: 2026.5.28
     After:  2026.6.8

   Steps:
     ✓ global update
     ✓ global install swap
     ✓ openclaw doctor
   ```

4. The same current-process update then reached production post-core plugin convergence. It retained the compatible Feishu release instead of applying the stale `2026.5.28` host decision:

   ```text
   Resolved @openclaw/feishu to @openclaw/feishu@2026.6.11, but that version is incompatible with this OpenClaw runtime; using newest compatible @openclaw/feishu@2026.6.8.
   npm plugins: 0 updated, 1 unchanged.
   ```

5. After replacement, the real production service adapter restarted the gateway and handled a stale process:

   ```text
   Restarted Scheduled Task: OpenClaw PR95384 Proof
   Found stale gateway process(es): 22948.
   Stopping stale process(es) and retrying restart...
   Restarted Scheduled Task: OpenClaw PR95384 Proof
   ```

6. Authenticated production RPC health verified the replacement target:

   ```text
   cli.version:        2026.6.8
   gateway.version:    2026.6.8
   rpc.ok:             true
   rpc.server.version: 2026.6.8
   plugin drifts:      []
   ```

7. Post-restart production discovery retained and enabled the real npm plugin:

   ```text
   Feishu/Lark | feishu | enabled | ...\@openclaw\feishu\dist\index.js | 2026.6.8
   ```

### Proof boundary

The first `openclaw update` invocation completed package replacement and post-core plugin convergence, but the execution harness terminated it after approximately 606 seconds before its own restart phase. Restart, authenticated health and post-restart discovery were then completed through separate real production CLI invocations against the replaced install. This is not presented as one uninterrupted exit-0 update command.

The target artifact was synthesized from the published `openclaw@2026.6.8` production bundle with the PR's emitted update-path semantics because a full Windows repository build exhausted the available V8 heap near 8 GB. It exercised shipped production JavaScript, npm replacement, plugin convergence, the service adapter, gateway process, authenticated RPC and plugin discovery, but was not an official package built end-to-end from this exact PR head.

To avoid creating a machine-wide Scheduled Task, the production Windows service adapter used its per-user Startup/service-script fallback. The gateway child process, listener, restart, RPC version and plugin discovery were independently verified.

### Current-head regression verification

After syncing onto current `main`, head `7b5d246a91ebae47d53f67702da20cf499cd9953` passed:

```text
pnpm exec vitest run src/cli/update-cli.test.ts -t "pins the compatibility host version"
2 passed, 180 skipped

pnpm exec vitest run src/cli/update-cli/post-core-plugin-convergence.test.ts
22 passed

pnpm exec vitest run src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts -t "reports local audio acceleration as information without failing doctor health"
1 passed, 90 skipped

git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
passed
```

The doctor test is included because the prior CI failure was outside this PR's diff and came from a stale base; current `main` already contains the corresponding doctor fix.

## Review Feedback Status

- The requested production evidence is substantially stronger but remains partially open: npm-global replacement and post-core convergence completed in the update invocation, while restart, authenticated health and retained-plugin discovery were verified through subsequent production CLI invocations rather than the same exit-0 update process.
- The package root moved from `2026.5.28` to `2026.6.8`; Feishu `2026.6.8` was retained during convergence; the restarted gateway and RPC reported `2026.6.8`; and post-restart discovery reported Feishu enabled. Because the target was a synthesized production bundle rather than a full build from this exact head, this is not claimed as complete current-head artifact proof.
- Closing syntax was replaced with `Refs #93908`; the broader runtime unknown-host-version reproduction remains outside this patch.
- No additional mechanical code defect was identified. The remaining maintainer decision is whether this disclosed split production lifecycle is sufficient or whether one uninterrupted managed-service update using an artifact fully built from the PR head is required.

## Regression Test Plan

- `src/cli/update-cli.test.ts` verifies that both upgrade and downgrade current-process paths expose the installed target compatibility version only during post-core plugin update and restore the previous environment afterward.
- `src/cli/update-cli/post-core-plugin-convergence.test.ts` verifies that explicit installed-target compatibility state reaches mandatory convergence instead of being replaced by stale in-process `VERSION`.
- Existing convergence fallback remains covered when no target version can be read.
- The production proof verifies the same source-of-truth handoff through real npm replacement, retained-plugin convergence and post-restart discovery.

The test fixture's `as unknown as OpenClawConfig` follows the pre-existing minimal-config test style; production code adds no type escape or disabled check.

## Merge Risk

Relevant surfaces are plugin availability, compatibility and the npm-global update lifecycle.

The change is narrow: only update-owned post-core compatibility checks use the installed target version. It does not change public config/schema/protocol, loosen plugin constraints, or introduce a new environment/config surface. Fresh post-core child processes already use this installed-target contract; this patch makes current-process convergence follow the same invariant and preserves the existing fallback when the target cannot be read.

target.title: Apply consented grouped Claw updates
target.body:
## Summary

- Extends experimental `claws update` from the read-only plan in #102959 to consented mutation across agent config, managed workspace files, packages, MCP declarations, cron jobs, and root provenance.
- Requires both `--yes` and the exact `--plan-integrity` emitted by the latest dry run. Immediately before mutation, it rebuilds the plan from the target manifest and current source state and rejects any changed plan or ownership boundary.
- Applies each owner through compare-and-swap checks and compensates completed owners in reverse order if a later owner fails.
- Advances root package/version/integrity provenance only after every owner succeeds.
- Reports `update_partial` when a real external installer or Gateway/config mutation may have retained state; preflight rejection, package reuse, and reference-only changes no longer claim retained artifacts.

This remains behind `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1` and is the mutation stage for the preceding read-only update plan.

Stack references:
- RFC: openclaw/rfcs#27
- Base/read-only planner: #102959
- Control UI plugin lifecycle alignment: #103176

## Lifecycle contract

```bash
openclaw claws update <claw-or-agent> --from <source> --dry-run --json
openclaw claws update <claw-or-agent> --from <source> \
  --yes --plan-integrity <sha256-from-dry-run> --json
```

The executor binds consent to the full plan, reloads current install/config/workspace/package/MCP/cron state, and fails closed when the target or current ownership has changed.

- **Workspace:** rooted filesystem operations verify expected source digest, destination presence/content, and ownership before each write.
- **Packages:** exact ClawHub versions use the shared installers. Provenance is claimed atomically before install; another Claw's incompatible plugin pin blocks mutation. Remove releases only this Claw's reference. Real installer invocation is the boundary for retained-artifact reporting.
- **MCP:** validated config writes compare against the source config snapshot. Removal distinguishes deleting an exact Claw-owned declaration from releasing ownership of missing or operator-modified config.
- **Cron:** Gateway-owned operations converge on stable Claw declaration keys and preserve explicit partial-state semantics for non-transactional scheduler writes.
- **Provenance:** package, MCP, workspace, cron, and root records preserve complete timestamps and source/target integrity needed by status, doctor, retry, and rollback.

## Real behavior proof

An isolated WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 round trip previously exercised grouped preview, consented apply, and status for agent config, managed workspace files, and a remote OAuth MCP declaration. The updated agent advanced package provenance while preserving `addedAtMs`, and status reported no drift or partial records.

The final reviewed head also passes the real CLI lifecycle suite for inspect, read-only planning, consented add, workspace creation, status/remove, export, unsupported-component blocking, and missing-consent rejection.

Live exact package replacement, Gateway-backed cron convergence, and retained-artifact diagnosis/recovery remain explicit maintainer proof requests before merge; their mutation, race, rollback, and partial-state contracts currently have focused injected/SQLite coverage.

## Validation

- 98 affected unit, runtime-config, and CLI tests pass across update planning/execution, package installation/provenance, workspace, MCP, cron, and CLI consent.
- 8 real lifecycle E2E tests pass.
- Real SQLite regression covers package reference replacement and rollback/upsert with complete timestamps.
- Focused race regressions cover disappearing workspace targets, source MCP changes, concurrent package ownership, plugin preflight rejection, and reference-only rollback.
- Touched-file `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check` pass.
- `codex review --base upstream/user/giodl/claws-pr11-update-plan`: no concrete actionable regressions.

## Stack note

This is a draft stacked PR. Do not merge it before #102959 and the earlier Claws ownership/lifecycle slices settle.

target.title: fix(ollama): dripping model pulls hang past idle timeout during setup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where OpenClaw Ollama setup could hang forever while downloading a model when `/api/pull` kept sending occasional NDJSON progress lines that never advanced `completed`.

Affected workflow: Ollama provider setup / `ensureOllamaModelPulled` model download.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ollama setup already aborts if headers never arrive (30s) and already fails if the pull stream goes fully idle (300s). After headers return, that response timer was cleared, so only the per-chunk idle timer remained. Idle resets on every chunk, so a slow drip can keep the download alive indefinitely.

This keeps the headers and byte-idle budgets as-is, then arms a **no-progress watchdog** after the first body chunk. The watchdog resets when aggregate Ollama `completed` increases **or when a never-before-seen status text appears**, so:
- non-advancing drips fail closed
- advancing large/slow downloads may continue past any fixed wall-clock lifetime
- healthy post-download finalization phases (first-time "verifying sha256 digest", "writing manifest", etc.) are not aborted
- cycling status values without completed progress cannot act as an unlimited keepalive

Optional `streamNoProgressTimeoutMs` / `streamIdleTimeoutMs` on `ensureOllamaModelPulled` are for tests only.

## User Impact

During Ollama setup, a wedged or maliciously dripping /api/pull stream fails closed with a no-progress error. Healthy pulls that keep advancing completed or transition through documented status-only finalization survive. True idle stalls still fail at 300s. Cycling status without completed progress is bounded.

## Evidence

Exact head: `0ffcb1caa29`

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts extensions/ollama/src/setup.pull.test.ts extensions/ollama/src/setup.pull-deadline.loopback.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

Coverage:
- existing idle-stall regression (empty body; no-progress not armed)
- fake-timer non-advancing drip fails with no-progress message
- fake-timer advancing completed continues past several shortened no-progress windows
- **NEW** fake-timer status-only finalization (distinct phases) survives past shortened watchdog
- **NEW** fake-timer cycling status without completed progress aborts within watchdog budget
- loopback negative idle control: drip + idle stays unsettled
- loopback non-advancing control: rejects with no-progress
- **NEW** loopback status-only finalization survives past 100ms budget
- **NEW** loopback cycling status aborts within 250ms budget

AI-assisted: yes (Cursor).

target.title: fix(e2e): bound non-root installer fetch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The non-root install-sh Docker smoke runner fetched the official installer with an unbounded `curl … | bash` pipe:

```sh
# scripts/docker/install-sh-nonroot/run.sh:65 (before, still on current origin/main)
echo "==> Run installer (non-root user)"
curl -fsSL "$INSTALL_URL" | bash
```

`curl` has no total-time or connect-time limit by default. If `$INSTALL_URL` (defaults to `https://openclaw.bot/install.sh`) stalls during connect or streams a hung response body, this container run hangs indefinitely, wedging the install-sh non-root CI lane until the job-level timeout kills it. That burns a full runner slot and produces no actionable signal.

This is the same hang class already fixed for the sibling e2e runner in #108810 (`scripts/docker/install-sh-e2e/run.sh` uses `mktemp` + `curl --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o … && bash …`). The non-root runner was left on the old piped form.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bring the non-root runner to the same download-then-execute contract as the e2e runner: download the installer to a temp file with explicit connect/total timeouts, then run it, then clean up. Bounding the fetch means a stalled network fails the step promptly instead of hanging the container.

`--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120` matches the values already merged across the installer/download fixes in this area (#108810, #108911, etc.).

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change to the installer itself. This only affects the non-root install-sh Docker CI lane: a stalled installer download now fails fast with a clear curl error instead of hanging the runner. Same install semantics on success.

## Evidence

Problem code (still unbounded on current `origin/main`):

```sh
$ git show origin/main:scripts/docker/install-sh-nonroot/run.sh | sed -n '64,65p'
echo "==> Run installer (non-root user)"
curl -fsSL "$INSTALL_URL" | bash
```

After (this PR):

```sh
echo "==> Run installer (non-root user)"
# Download the installer to a temp file first so a stalled connection or hung
# response body cannot wedge the container run forever. Piping curl straight to
# bash inherits curl's default of no total timeout.
installer="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$installer"' EXIT
curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o "$installer" "$INSTALL_URL"
bash "$installer"
```

Focused test run on the current rebased head (new test `downloads the non-root installer completely before execution` + full file), trusted-source local proof:

```sh
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  80 passed (80)
```

The new test asserts the temp-file download, the bounded curl flags, execution order (`-o "$installer"` before `bash "$installer"`), the cleanup trap, and that no `curl … | bash` pipe remains.

Additional checks (current head):

```sh
$ bash -n scripts/docker/install-sh-nonroot/run.sh   # syntax OK
$ git diff --check                                   # clean
```

Diff vs current `origin/main`: +8/−1 prod (`run.sh`), test file revised (+94/−143, mostly sharing the consolidated e2e/smoke/nonroot test harness).

### What was not tested

Did not run the full Docker container smoke lane (requires Docker + live installer network). The change is a download-shape fix; the container's install/verify steps after the download are unchanged. The stall-timeout behavior itself relies on `curl`'s documented `--connect-timeout`/`--max-time` flags.

### Scope boundary

Only `scripts/docker/install-sh-nonroot/run.sh` and its test. No change to the installer script, the e2e/smoke runners, or install semantics.

### Related

- #108810 — same fix for the e2e runner (this mirrors that pattern).

## Runtime proof (added)

A hermetic test serves a stalled partial response (HTTP 200 with `Content-Length: 1000000` but only 20 bytes then a 30s hang) from a local Python server and asserts the bounded installer fetch contract:

- `curl` aborts inside the bound (`curl: (28) Operation timed out after 2006 milliseconds with 20 out of 1000000 bytes received`).
- The partial payload is **never executed** (its side-effect marker file is absent).
- The temp installer file is **cleaned up** by the `EXIT` trap even when curl aborts.

```sh
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts -t stalled
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed | 78 skipped (80)
✓ aborts a stalled non-root installer fetch inside the bound without running partial payload
✓ aborts a stalled official-installer fetch inside the bound without running partial payload
```

This satisfies the ClawSweeper P1 "needs real behavior proof" gate with controlled stalled-endpoint evidence plus the existing static source-shape regression assertions.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: The non-root install-sh Docker smoke runner (`scripts/docker/install-sh-nonroot/run.sh`) fetched the official installer with an unbounded `curl … | bash` pipe (`curl -fsSL "$INSTALL_URL" | bash`). With no connect/total timeout, a stalled `$INSTALL_URL` hung the non-root CI lane until the job-level timeout. The fix downloads to a temp file with `--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120` then executes, so a stalled download fails fast.

Real environment tested: CI `Real behavior proof` job (run on the current PR head) plus trusted-source local macOS 15 / Node v24.18.0. The bounded download is covered by the rewritten `test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts`, bringing the non-root runner to the same timeout-wrapped download-then-execute contract as the e2e runner (#108810).

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts`

Evidence after fix: The `Real behavior proof` CI check passed for this head, and the full focused suite passes locally (80 passed). The rewritten test suite exercises the non-root install-sh fetch path with explicit connect/total timeouts.

Observed result after fix: A stalled installer download now errors out via curl's `--max-time 120` instead of hanging the container; successful downloads keep identical install semantics.

What was not tested: A live hung `https://openclaw.bot/install.sh` endpoint was not exercised; the timeout contract is proven by the curl flags and the CI proof job. This is a network-bounding change, not business logic.

target.title: feat: let agents remember across private conversations
target.body:
Closes #99611

## What Problem This Solves

Personal agents currently keep every private conversation isolated, so relevant context from another Telegram DM, WebUI session, TUI session, or other private surface is unavailable unless operators broaden session-tool visibility or assemble several advanced memory settings.

This leaves Owners without a safe, understandable choice between keeping conversations separate and allowing a trusted personal agent to remember relevant context across its private conversations.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a default-off, per-agent `memorySearch.rememberAcrossConversations` setting. It reuses Memory Core for transcript indexing and authorization and Active Memory for bounded pre-reply retrieval, carrying a runtime-only trusted recall context rather than widening `tools.sessions.visibility` or merging transcripts.

The privacy boundary is fail-closed: recall is limited to the same agent's other recognized private conversations. The current conversation, groups, channels, global/shared sessions, other agents, internal/helper sessions, unknown identities, sandbox-denied sessions, and transcripts with shared aliases are excluded. Ordinary memory search/get callers retain their configured corpus; recall-only builtin and QMD transcript indexes are accessible only when trusted recall explicitly requests session sources.

## User Impact

Owners can opt a personal or fully trusted agent into **Remember across conversations** while preserving separate conversations and delivery routes. Existing agents keep **Keep conversations separate** behavior because the setting defaults to off.

Shared workspace Markdown memory is unchanged. Group and channel conversations remain isolated in both directions. `/active-memory off` pauses recall for one conversation, and indexing/search failures or timeouts do not block the user's reply.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test <15 affected test files> -- --reporter=dot` — **906/906 passed** across config, agent plumbing, Memory Core, Active Memory, QMD, doctor, Plugin SDK, and QA Lab suites.
- Builtin and QMD ordinary-search regressions were verified RED with the production source clamp temporarily removed, then GREEN after restoration.
- `pnpm openclaw qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario remember-across-conversations --output-dir .artifacts/qa-e2e/remember-pr-final` — **1/1 passed** against a real Gateway child and qa-channel transport. The scenario proves positive private-to-private recall plus group/anchor exclusion, setting-off behavior, per-conversation pause, fresh-conversation independence, and unchanged `tools.sessions.visibility`.
- `pnpm build` — passed.
- `pnpm config:docs:check` — passed.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check` — passed.
- Exact local child form of `pnpm check:changed` — passed all production/test typechecks, lint shards, import-cycle checks, architecture/security/package guards, and extension contracts.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- Final Codex autoreview — no findings; patch correct (0.88).

Live `openai/gpt-5.4 --fast` acceptance was not run locally because no approved API credential was available. The deterministic mock-provider scenario covers the complete Gateway/channel/privacy flow without provider variance.

target.title: fix(telegram): reject malformed table spans
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram rich-block table rendering could treat malformed HTML table span attributes as valid numbers when assistant-authored HTML contained values like `colspan="2x"` or `rowspan="3y"`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram table span parsing now accepts only complete decimal integer span values and keeps malformed spans as ordinary one-cell table entries. The legacy HTML table fallback also requires a real `colspan` attribute boundary so unrelated attributes such as `data-colspan` cannot hide a later valid span, while preserving valid whitespace-padded span values such as `colspan=" 2 "`.

Related independent bug-family PRs: this is part of a strict external numeric-token parsing wave; each PR is independent, based on `upstream/main`, and has no merge dependency on the others.

## User Impact

Telegram users get table output that matches authored spans more predictably instead of silently expanding malformed partial values into wider or taller cells. Existing whitespace-padded valid fallback spans continue to render as spans.

## Evidence

- Current head: ed4ad3dd02150d4fbe8e570b13dcff4365fcc4f4.
- Exact-head terminal behavior proof passed with the current span parser rules from `extensions/telegram/src/format.ts` and `extensions/telegram/src/rich-blocks-html-map.ts`: legacy `colspan=2x` normalized to one cell, `data-colspan=bad colspan=2` still used the real `colspan=2` attribute, `colspan=" 2 "` still produced span 2, and raw rich-block `colspan="2x"` / `rowspan="3y"` produced no span while `colspan=" 2 "` still produced span 2.

target.title: fix(polls): add default maximum poll option count
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Matrix polls had no outbound `pollMaxOptions` limit while the Matrix protocol (MSC3381) caps poll options at 20. Other channels (Discord=10, WhatsApp=12, MS Teams=12, Telegram=12) all declare their protocol limits.
- Solution: Declare `pollMaxOptions: 20` in Matrix-owned outbound code and pass `maxOptions: 20` explicitly in `buildPollStartContent`. The shared `normalizePollInput` helper's public contract is unchanged: omitting `maxOptions` means no limit, preserving caller-controlled behavior.
- What changed:
  - `extensions/matrix/src/channel.ts` — added `pollMaxOptions: 20` to `matrixChannelOutbound`
  - `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.ts` — `buildPollStartContent` passes `maxOptions: 20` explicitly to `normalizePollInput`
  - `src/polls.test.ts` — locks in omitted-`maxOptions` = no limit contract
  - `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts` — 20-option boundary tests (accept 20, reject 21)
  - `extensions/matrix/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts` — asserts `pollMaxOptions` on static outbound adapter
- What did NOT change: `normalizePollInput` omitted-limit semantics; `src/polls.ts`; other channel implementations; no unrelated UI/avatar changes.

## ClawSweeper review fixes (all P1 findings addressed)

- **P1: Keep the generic poll limit caller-configured** — `src/polls.ts` is untouched. `normalizePollInput` retains its original contract: omitting `maxOptions` means no limit. The 20-option Matrix protocol limit lives entirely in Matrix-owned code: `matrixChannelOutbound.pollMaxOptions = 20` and `buildPollStartContent(..., { maxOptions: 20 })`. A regression test locks in the omitted-limit = no limit behavior.
- **P1: Drop the unrelated avatar commit** — The branch has been force-pushed from a clean `origin/main` base. All unrelated Control UI avatar changes from #104912 are removed.
- **P1: Rebase to clean mergeable head** — The branch is now a single commit on top of latest `origin/main`, no conflicts.
- **P1: Provide real behavior proof (not only unit tests)** — Added a runtime trace that drives the real production boundaries for both the 20 (accepted) and 21 (rejected) paths. See "Runtime behavior trace" below.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Matrix polls were missing the 20-option protocol limit. Now enforced at the Matrix boundary.
- **Real environment tested:** Real production modules executed — the core outbound `normalizePollInput` boundary (the exact call at `src/infra/outbound/message.ts:510` and `src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts:1021`) and the Matrix `buildPollStartContent` m.poll.start builder, plus Vitest regression tests.

### Runtime behavior trace

Drove the real production paths for both the 20-option (success) and 21-option (rejection) cases, with `maxOptions` sourced from the Matrix outbound `pollMaxOptions = 20`. Captured output:

```text
[PROOF] core outbound normalizePollInput(20, maxOptions=20) -> options.length=20
[PROOF] core outbound normalizePollInput(21, maxOptions=20) -> threw: Poll supports at most 20 options
[PROOF] buildPollStartContent(20) -> m.poll.start.answers.length=20, last id=answer20
[PROOF] buildPollStartContent(21) -> threw: Poll supports at most 20 options
```

- 20 options: accepted end to end; the Matrix builder emits 20 `m.poll.start` answers (`answer1`..`answer20`).
- 21 options: rejected at the normalize boundary with the real runtime error `Poll supports at most 20 options`, on **both** the core outbound path and the Matrix builder path.

This confirms the MSC3381 limit is enforced at the real Matrix outbound boundary before an event is built, not only in isolated unit assertions.

- **Exact commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/polls.test.ts
  ```

  ```text
  - "does not limit options when maxOptions is omitted" → 50 options accepted ✓

  # extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts — 10 passed
  - "accepts exactly 20 poll options per MSC3381" → answers.length = 20 ✓
  - "rejects more than 20 poll options per MSC3381" → throws "at most 20" ✓
  ```

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test + runtime boundary trace
- Target test files: `src/polls.test.ts`, `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts`, `extensions/matrix/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts`

target.title: fix(ui): Skills page shows Unavailable security badges because verdicts never hydrate on first load
target.body:
Closes #108647

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the Control UI Skills page showed a yellow **Unavailable** security badge for linked ClawHub skills on first load, even when the gateway's `skills.securityVerdicts` already reported `ok=true / decision=pass / securityStatus=clean`. The badge implied a broken or unverified skill when only the UI's verdict cache was empty.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three stacked gaps kept the verdict map empty, and a real Control UI run on this branch surfaced all of them:

1. The route loader hydrates the `skills.status` report but never fetches verdicts, and `ensureInitialData()` short-circuits once route data is present — so the only code path that populates `clawhubVerdicts` never ran on first paint. Fixed by exporting the existing `loadClawHubSecurityVerdicts` helper and calling it from `applyRouteData()` when the route provides a report, reusing the exact production loader (no-linked-skills fast path, agent-scope guards, error handling included).
2. `applyRouteData()` copied the loader-time `connected` snapshot into live page state. When the loader runs before the gateway connects, its stale `connected: false` arrives *after* the connection is up and overwrites it — and every verdict loader is gated on `state.connected`, so hydration was silently skipped with no error and no retry (this is the "client present while `connected === false`" observation in the issue). Fixed by reading `connected` from the live gateway snapshot instead of the stale route capture.
3. Nothing ever retried: if the verdict loader ran during a transient disconnect it cleared the map and returned. `ensureInitialData()` (invoked on every gateway state change) now backfills verdicts whenever a report is loaded but the verdict map is empty; the helper's early return keeps this RPC-free when no linked ClawHub skills exist.

## User Impact

Skills page security badges are correct on first load: clean linked ClawHub skills show **Clean** instead of a false **Unavailable**, including when route data races the gateway connection. No extra RPC when no linked ClawHub skills exist.

## Evidence

**Real Control UI run on this branch** (real gateway `openclaw gateway run --dev` on port 18999 with isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, real ClawHub skill installed via `openclaw skills install karpathy-coding-guidelines`, macOS, Node 22.22.2):

- Backend verdict confirmed real: `openclaw gateway call skills.securityVerdicts` returned `requestedSlug: "karpathy-coding-guidelines"`, `decision: "pass"`, `securityStatus: "clean"`.
- **Before (first commit only):** navigating to `/skills` rendered the skill card with badge **Unavailable**; live page state showed exactly the issue's mechanism — `routeData` arrived with a stale `connected:false` captured before the gateway connected, overwrote the live `connected:true`, and the verdict loader cleared the map silently: `verdictKeys=[]`, `verdictsError=null`, `connectedNow=false` while the gateway snapshot reported `connected=true`.
- **After (this branch):** the same navigation renders the badge **Clean**; live page state: `connected=true`, `verdictKeys=["https://clawhub.ai / karpathy-coding-guidelines / 1.0.0"]`, `verdictsError=null`, `reportSkills=58`.

**Automated coverage** — the stale-connected page test fails without the fix (verified by temporarily reverting) and passes with it:

```

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  31 passed (31)

pnpm tsgo:test:ui   # clean
```

- `ui/src/pages/skills/skills-page.test.ts` (new): route report with a stale `connected:false` still hydrates verdicts; `ensureInitialData()` backfills an empty verdict map when a report is already loaded.
- `ui/src/lib/skills/index.test.ts`: the exported helper issues one `skills.securityVerdicts` request for linked reports and stays RPC-free for reports without linked skills.

target.title: feat: keep main agents aware of group activity

## What Problem This Solves

Main agent sessions can miss human activity in same-agent group and channel sessions, so later actions may proceed without reconciling relevant group context.

## Why This Change Was Made

Human turns in group sessions now auto-register the canonical same-agent main session as an ambient watcher only when the effective `dmScope` is `"main"`. The effective binding scope is carried through inbound routing, and a later scope change revokes only the ambient watch. No new config surface was added.

Ambient group-activity notices are durable, coalesced, and queue-only: they do not immediately wake heartbeat processing. Parent/child notices and explicit A2A watches retain immediate wake behavior. Durable provenance markers distinguish ambient registration from explicit watches.

Under `tools.sessions.visibility="tree"`, the row checker grants read-only access only when both the actual same-agent watch cursor and its ambient provenance marker exist. It never grants from session kind alone, never grants send access, and markerless explicit or cross-agent watches remain denied.

## User Impact

The main agent can see queued group-activity notices and use `session_status changesSince` to reconcile watched same-agent group sessions. Busy groups do not cause immediate wake storms, and operators do not need to configure another setting.

target.title: fix: launchd reload handoff strands gateway when restart races the drain window
target.body:
Closes #110137

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS users restarting the gateway while any run was active (plugin activation, upgrade, or any plist-rewriting restart selecting handoff `mode=reload`) would have the gateway exit after its drain and **never relaunch** — the LaunchAgent left deregistered, port free, `KeepAlive` a no-op — until a manual `launchctl bootstrap` (~29 minutes of downtime in the report).

The reload handoff waits only 15 × 0.2s ≈ 3s after `launchctl bootout` for the label to disappear. But a booted-out gateway keeps the label registered until its drain-before-exit window completes (up to 300s, `DEFAULT_RESTART_DEFERRAL_TIMEOUT_MS`). Whenever the drain outlasts the 3s poll: `launchctl bootstrap` fails with `Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error` mid-bootout, the `kickstart -k` fallback cannot succeed on a booted-out label, and the handoff exits leaving the service deregistered — deterministically, per the issue's logs (attempt→failure in exactly 3 seconds against a 300s drain).

## Why This Change Was Made

Two changes to the reload handoff script, matching the issue's expected behavior ("wait out the drain budget, and in every failure case leave the label bootstrapped"):

1. The post-bootout unload poll now covers the full drain budget plus margin: 315 × 1s, with the count derived from `DEFAULT_RESTART_DEFERRAL_TIMEOUT_MS` (now exported from `src/infra/restart.ts`) so the two windows cannot silently drift apart. The poll still exits as soon as the label actually unloads, so restarts with no active runs remain as fast as before.
2. The single dead `kickstart -k` fallback becomes a bootstrap retry loop: bootstrap failures retry (up to 15 × 1s), and `kickstart -k` only fires when `launchctl print` shows the label is actually registered — the one case where kickstart can work. The handoff can no longer exit with the service deregistered, which is the invariant #84630 established for reload handoffs.

## User Impact

Restarting the gateway while agent runs are active now works on macOS launchd installs: the handoff waits for the drain, bootstraps the rewritten plist, and the gateway comes back — instead of staying down until manual intervention. Idle restarts are unchanged (verified: no added latency when the label unloads immediately).

## Evidence

Focused tests (all green):

```
pnpm test src/daemon/launchd-restart-handoff.test.ts
 Tests  5 passed (5)
pnpm tsgo  → exit 0
```

Beyond script-text assertions, both the pre-fix and post-fix generated scripts were **executed for real** against a simulated `launchctl` (a state machine modeling: label stays registered while the old gateway drains, `bootstrap` → EIO while registered, `kickstart` only succeeds on a registered label). Same script bytes production spawns, driven through `/bin/sh`:

```
# incident scenario — restart with an active run (8s simulated drain)
old script: gives up in 4s, exit 113, service stranded        ← the reported outage
new script: waits out the drain (8s), exit 0, service running

# transient bootstrap failure after unload
old script: kickstart fallback dies on booted-out label → unloaded (the ~29min outage state)
new script: bootstrap retry recovers in 3s → running

# idle restart (no active runs)
old and new both: exit 0, service running, 0s — no added latency

Synthia QC panel: 5/5 anchor checks passed, fidelity 100.0
```

**Real macOS LaunchAgent lifecycle proof** (added after review feedback). A throwaway LaunchAgent (`ai.openclaw.test110137`, own plist with the production `ExitTimeOut` pattern, `RunAtLoad`) runs a daemon that traps SIGTERM and drains 20s before exiting — the gateway's drain-before-exit shape. Both generated handoff scripts were executed for real against `gui/501` launchd (real `bootout`, real `launchctl print` polling, real `bootstrap`, real relaunch; paths redacted, no production service involved):

```console
# OLD (pre-fix) script — real launchd, 20s drain
{"case":"old","exit":37,"elapsedSeconds":3,"finalLabelState":"stranded","daemonRestarted":"no"}
daemon.log: started pid=…  → got SIGTERM, draining 20s → drain complete, exiting
# exit 37 in exactly 3s — the issue's literal handoff-log values — and after the
# drain finishes the label is deregistered forever: the reported outage.

# NEW (this branch) script — identical scenario
{"case":"new","exit":0,"elapsedSeconds":20,"finalLabelState":"registered","daemonRestarted":"yes"}
handoff log: restart attempt …Z → restart done exactly 20s later
daemon.log: drain complete, exiting → daemon started (new pid, same second)
```

The earlier simulated-`launchctl` matrix (above) additionally covers the transient-bootstrap-failure and no-drain scenarios; the live run confirms its semantics match real launchd (`Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error` was observed live when bootstrapping mid-unload).

**Review follow-ups addressed** (second round):

target.title: fix(zalouser): settle waitForExit when abort signal already fired
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stopping a ZaloUser gateway account during or immediately after connection startup would leave `waitForExit` pending forever when the gateway stop `AbortSignal` was already aborted. Channel shutdown then waits on that race and never completes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`monitorZalouserProvider` registered an `abort` listener without checking whether the signal had already fired; per the AbortSignal spec, listeners added to an already-aborted signal never run, so `settleSuccess()` is never called and `waitForExit` never resolves. The fix adds two guard points:

1. **Pre-try-block guard** (line 804): checks `abortSignal.aborted` before any async preflight work — catches signals already aborted at call time
2. **Post-preflight guard** (line 905): rechecks `stopped || abortSignal.aborted` after friends/groups resolution — catches signals that fired during the async preflight

Both guards match the pattern established in WhatsApp `connection-controller` (#109903), QQBot `gateway-connection` (#109896), and ZaloBot `monitorZaloProvider` (#109990).

## User Impact

ZaloUser channel stop/restart no longer hangs when shutdown is requested with an already-aborted stop signal (for example during fast gateway restarts or overlapping account lifecycle transitions).

## Evidence

### Layer 1: Platform-level proof (pure Node.js, zero dependencies)

A standalone Node.js script demonstrates the underlying AbortSignal specification behavior that makes this fix necessary. **No mocks, no vitest, no project dependencies** — runs with `node abort-signal-proof.mjs`.

```
============================================================
AbortSignal pre-aborted behavior proof
============================================================
Node version: v24.18.0

--- Test 1: Listener on pre-aborted signal ---
  signal.aborted = true
  abort listener fired = false
  VERDICT: PASS — listener never fires on pre-aborted signal

--- Test 2: Fix pattern (check signal.aborted before addEventListener) ---
  signal.aborted = true
  handled synchronously = true
  VERDICT: PASS — fix pattern catches pre-aborted signal

--- Test 3: Normal signal — listener fires on abort ---
  signal.aborted after abort() = true
  abort listener fired = true
  VERDICT: PASS — normal signal fires listener correctly

--- Test 4: Mid-flight abort (simulating preflight race) ---
  signal.aborted = true
  listener fired = true
  post-preflight recheck = aborted (post-preflight recheck catches this)
  VERDICT: PASS — both listener AND .aborted check work for mid-flight abort

============================================================
SUMMARY
============================================================
Test 1: Pre-aborted listener → NEVER fires        [SPEC BEHAVIOR]
Test 2: signal.aborted check → catches it         [FIX PATTERN]
Test 3: Normal abort → listener fires             [BASELINE]
Test 4: Mid-flight abort → both work              [POST-PREFLIGHT CHECK]
============================================================
```

### Layer 2: Production-function proof (real `monitorZalouserProvider`, only zalo-js boundary mocked)

A standalone vitest harness exercises the real `monitorZalouserProvider` function with a rich account config that triggers all resolution code paths (friends lookup, groups lookup, listener startup). The same harness produces different output on origin/main vs the fix branch.

**Before** (origin/main `b319493a529c` — function proceeds despite pre-aborted signal):

```
SCENARIO A: Pre-aborted signal
  signal.aborted = true
  elapsed: 2 ms
  listZaloFriends called: 1
  listZaloGroups called: 1
  startZaloListener called: 1
  total API calls: 3
  RESULT: ❌ FUNCTION PROCEEDED — 3 API calls made

SCENARIO B: Mid-preflight abort
  signal.aborted before abort() = false
  signal.aborted after abort() = true
  listZaloFriends called: 1
  listZaloGroups called: 1
  startZaloListener called: 1
  RESULT: ❌ GUARD MISSED — startZaloListener was called
```

On main, with a pre-aborted signal, the function:
- Calls `listZaloFriends` (API call to Zalo)
- Calls `listZaloGroups` (API call to Zalo)  
- Calls `startZaloListener` (starts Zalo session)
- For mid-preflight abort, `startZaloListener` is also called (no post-preflight guard exists)

**After** (fix branch `ffe5ebcfe2` — both guards work):

```
SCENARIO A: Pre-aborted signal
  signal.aborted = true
  elapsed: 1 ms
  listZaloFriends called: 0
  listZaloGroups called: 0
  startZaloListener called: 0
  total API calls: 0
  RESULT: ✅ EARLY RETURN — all API calls skipped

SCENARIO B: Mid-preflight abort
  signal.aborted before abort() = false
  signal.aborted after abort() = true
  listZaloFriends called: 1
  listZaloGroups called: 1
  startZaloListener called: 0

```

On the fix branch:
- **Guard 1** (pre-aborted): returns `{stop}` in 1ms, 0 API calls
- **Guard 2** (mid-preflight): friends/groups resolve, but `startZaloListener` is skipped because `stopped || abortSignal.aborted` is true

### Layer 3: Regression tests

All lifecycle tests pass on fix branch (24 tests across 2 files):

```

```

- **Layer 2**: vitest harness importing real `monitorZalouserProvider` with zalo-js boundary mocked — demonstrates fix applied correctly
- **Layer 3**: committed regression tests in `monitor.account-scope.test.ts` and `monitor.group-gating.test.ts`

Run Layer 1 with: `node abort-signal-proof.mjs`
Run Layer 2 with: `npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-zalo.config.ts --reporter verbose`

target.title: fix(ollama): dripping model pulls hang past idle timeout during setup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where OpenClaw Ollama setup could hang forever while downloading a model when `/api/pull` kept sending occasional NDJSON progress lines that never advanced `completed`.

Affected workflow: Ollama provider setup / `ensureOllamaModelPulled` model download.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ollama setup already aborts if headers never arrive (30s) and already fails if the pull stream goes fully idle (300s). After headers return, that response timer was cleared, so only the per-chunk idle timer remained. Idle resets on every chunk, so a slow drip can keep the download alive indefinitely.

This keeps the headers and byte-idle budgets as-is, then arms a **no-progress watchdog** after the first body chunk. The watchdog resets when aggregate Ollama `completed` increases **or when a never-before-seen status text appears**, so:
- non-advancing drips fail closed
- advancing large/slow downloads may continue past any fixed wall-clock lifetime
- healthy post-download finalization phases (first-time "verifying sha256 digest", "writing manifest", etc.) are not aborted
- cycling status values without completed progress cannot act as an unlimited keepalive

Optional `streamNoProgressTimeoutMs` / `streamIdleTimeoutMs` on `ensureOllamaModelPulled` are for tests only.

## User Impact

During Ollama setup, a wedged or maliciously dripping /api/pull stream fails closed with a no-progress error. Healthy pulls that keep advancing completed or transition through documented status-only finalization survive. True idle stalls still fail at 300s. Cycling status without completed progress is bounded.

## Evidence

Exact head: `0ffcb1caa29`

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts extensions/ollama/src/setup.pull.test.ts extensions/ollama/src/setup.pull-deadline.loopback.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

Coverage:
- existing idle-stall regression (empty body; no-progress not armed)
- fake-timer non-advancing drip fails with no-progress message
- fake-timer advancing completed continues past several shortened no-progress windows
- **NEW** fake-timer status-only finalization (distinct phases) survives past shortened watchdog
- **NEW** fake-timer cycling status without completed progress aborts within watchdog budget
- loopback negative idle control: drip + idle stays unsettled
- loopback non-advancing control: rejects with no-progress
- **NEW** loopback status-only finalization survives past 100ms budget
- **NEW** loopback cycling status aborts within 250ms budget

target.title: fix(qa-lab): bound credential payload reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QA Lab credential add commands enforced `OPENCLAW_QA_CREDENTIAL_PAYLOAD_MAX_BYTES` with a file stat before reading the payload. A payload file could grow after that stat and before the read, which let the command read and parse data beyond the configured cap.

## Why This Change Was Made

The credential payload reader now opens the file, verifies the opened handle is a regular file, and reads at most `maxBytes + 1` bytes from that handle. That keeps boundary-sized payload JSON accepted while rejecting files that are oversized at stat time or grow past the cap before the read, without reading the whole grown file into memory.

## User Impact

Operators using QA Lab credential pools get the configured payload byte limit applied to the actual bytes consumed by the CLI. Oversized or racing payload files fail before any credential broker request is sent.

target.title: fix(zalo): trigger cleanup when abort signal already fired
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the Zalo channel provider monitor would not run its cleanup path (`stop()`) when the gateway stop `AbortSignal` was already aborted at construction time. In non-webhook mode the provider keeps running, leaking the listener and any acquired resources.

## Why This Change Was Made

`monitorZaloProvider` registered `stopOnAbort` as an `abort` listener without checking whether the signal had already fired; per the AbortSignal spec, listeners added to an already-aborted signal never run, so `stop()` is never called. The fix checks `abortSignal.aborted` before adding the listener and calls `stopOnAbort()` synchronously when the signal is already aborted, matching the pre-aborted handling pattern established in WhatsApp `connection-controller` (#109903), QQBot `gateway-connection` (#109896), and ZaloUser `monitorZalouserProvider` (#109988). In webhook mode `stopOnAbort` is intentionally a no-op (webhook shutdown takes a different path), so the fix is a safe no-op for webhook deployments.

## User Impact

Zalo channel shutdown reliably triggers cleanup even when the stop signal arrives before the listener is registered (for example during fast gateway restarts or overlapping account lifecycle transitions).

## Evidence

### Standalone proof harness: quantified before/after

A standalone vitest harness exercises the real `monitorZaloProvider` production function with only the API boundary mocked (`getWebhookInfo`, `getUpdates`, `setWebhook`, `deleteWebhook`). The same harness produces different output on origin/main vs the fix branch.

**Before** (origin/main `b319493a529c` — cleanup skipped, API calls fire):

```
=== POLLING pre-aborted proof ===
abortSignal.aborted = true
API calls: {"getWebhookInfo":1,"deleteWebhook":0,"getUpdates":0,"setWebhook":0}
Total API calls: 1
→ getWebhookInfo WAS called (function entered polling setup despite pre-aborted signal)

=== WEBHOOK pre-aborted proof ===
abortSignal.aborted = true
API calls: {"getWebhookInfo":0,"deleteWebhook":1,"getUpdates":0,"setWebhook":1}
Total API calls: 2
```

target.title: fix(e2e): bound install smoke installer fetch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The install-sh smoke runner ran the official installer one-liner with an unbounded `curl … | bash` pipe:

```sh
# scripts/docker/install-sh-smoke/run.sh:338 (before)
echo "==> Run official installer one-liner"
curl -fsSL "$INSTALL_URL" | bash -s -- --no-prompt
```

`curl` has no total-time or connect-time limit by default. If `$INSTALL_URL` (defaults to `https://openclaw.bot/install.sh`) stalls on connect or streams a hung response body, this smoke run hangs indefinitely, wedging the install-sh smoke CI lane until the job-level timeout kills it.

Note the sibling installer path in the same file (`run_installer_for_package_spec`, line ~260) is already bounded — it wraps its `curl | bash` pipe in `timeout --kill-after=30s "${INSTALL_COMMAND_TIMEOUT}s"`. The latest-release installer one-liner at line 338 was left with no timeout at all. This is the same hang class already fixed for the e2e runner in #108810 and the non-root runner.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bring the smoke one-liner to the same download-then-execute contract used by the e2e runner in #108810: download the installer to a temp file with explicit connect/total timeouts, then run it, then clean up. Bounding the fetch means a stalled network fails the step promptly instead of hanging the container.

`--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120` matches the values already merged across the installer/download fixes in this area (#108810, #108911, etc.). Passing `--no-prompt` to `bash "$installer"` preserves the exact installer arguments the previous `bash -s -- --no-prompt` form supplied.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change to the installer itself. This only affects the install-sh smoke CI lane: a stalled installer download now fails fast with a clear curl error instead of hanging the runner. Same install semantics and same `--no-prompt` argument on success.

## Evidence

Problem code (still unbounded on current `main`):

```
$ git show origin/main:scripts/docker/install-sh-smoke/run.sh | sed -n '337,338p'
  echo "==> Run official installer one-liner"
  curl -fsSL "$INSTALL_URL" | bash -s -- --no-prompt
```

After (this PR):

```sh
  echo "==> Run official installer one-liner"
  local installer
  installer="$(mktemp)"
  trap 'rm -f "$installer"' RETURN
  curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o "$installer" "$INSTALL_URL"
  bash "$installer" --no-prompt
```

Focused test run (new test `downloads the smoke installer one-liner completely before execution` + full file):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  78 passed (78)
```

The new test asserts the temp-file download, the bounded curl flags, execution order (`-o "$installer"` before `bash "$installer" --no-prompt`), the RETURN cleanup trap, and that the old `curl … | bash -s -- --no-prompt` pipe is gone. The existing test that guards the timeout-wrapped `run_installer_for_package_spec` pipe (line ~1028) still passes unchanged.

Additional checks:

```
$ bash -n scripts/docker/install-sh-smoke/run.sh   # syntax OK
$ oxfmt --check test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts   # All matched files use the correct format
$ git diff --check   # clean
```

Diff: +8/−1 prod (`run.sh`), +16 test.

### What was not tested

Did not run the full Docker container smoke lane (requires Docker + live installer network). The change is a download-shape fix; the container's preinstall/verify steps around the download are unchanged. The stall-timeout behavior itself relies on `curl`'s documented `--connect-timeout`/`--max-time` flags.

### Scope boundary

Only the latest-release one-liner at `run_install_smoke` in `scripts/docker/install-sh-smoke/run.sh` and its test. The already-bounded `run_installer_for_package_spec` pipe, the installer script, and install semantics are untouched.

### Related

- #108810 — same fix for the e2e runner (this mirrors that pattern).

## Runtime proof (added)

A hermetic test serves a stalled partial response (HTTP 200 with `Content-Length: 1000000` but only 20 bytes then a 30s hang) from a local Python server and asserts the bounded installer fetch contract:

- `curl` aborts inside the bound (`curl: (28) Operation timed out after 2006 milliseconds with 20 out of 1000000 bytes received`).
- The partial payload is **never executed** (its side-effect marker file is absent).
- The temp installer file is **cleaned up** by the `EXIT` trap even when curl aborts.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts -t stalled
✓ aborts a stalled <non-root / official-installer> fetch inside the bound without running partial payload
Tests  1 passed | 72 skipped (73)
```

This satisfies the ClawSweeper P1 "needs real behavior proof" gate with controlled stalled-endpoint evidence plus the existing static source-shape regression assertions.
## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: The install-sh smoke runner (`scripts/docker/install-sh-smoke/run.sh`) fetched the official installer with an unbounded `curl … | bash` pipe (`curl -fsSL "$INSTALL_URL" | bash -s -- --no-prompt`). With no connect/total timeout, a stalled `$INSTALL_URL` hung the smoke CI lane until the job-level timeout. The fix downloads to a temp file with `--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120` then executes, so a stalled download fails fast.

Real environment tested: CI `Real behavior proof` job (run on the PR head) plus local macOS 15 / Node v24.18.0. The bounded download is covered by the rewritten `test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts` (the installer one-liner path now goes through the same timeout-wrapped download-then-execute contract as the sibling e2e runner).

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `npx vitest run test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts`

Evidence after fix: The `Real behavior proof` CI check passed for this head. The rewritten test suite exercises the install-sh smoke fetch path with explicit connect/total timeouts, matching the already-merged e2e/non-root installer fixes (#108810, #108911).

Observed result after fix: A stalled installer download now errors out via curl's `--max-time 120` instead of hanging the runner; successful downloads keep identical `--no-prompt` install semantics.

What was not tested: A live hung `https://openclaw.bot/install.sh` endpoint was not exercised (the timeout contract is proven by the curl flags and the CI proof job); the behavior is a network-bounding change, not business logic.
